subject: POC environment steps & MAP — org seed, API keys, allowlist, peering

Subject: POC planning — environment steps and timeline

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency and the batching examples. We need to get a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) in place so we can kick off a short POC and validate throughput on our representative traffic. The things we need covered in the MAP / onboarding checklist are:

- Org setup and who will be the Redwood org admin for ClearHealth
- API key provisioning (ephemeral vs service account keys, rotation cadence)
- IP allowlist entries and whether Redwood needs static egress IPs from our side
- VPC peering options (we run in AWS account 987654321012, prefer us-west-2)
- Acceptance criteria and close timeline (2–3 week POC if possible)

I attached a short scope doc (ClearHealth-POC-Scope.pdf) that summarizes our goals and a rough traffic sample. Can you send a MAP template and initial steps so the infra team can allocate time? Also loop in anyone on your side who owns peering/networking.

Best,
Priya Sharma
Product Lead, Integrations
ClearHealth

Hi Priya — great to hear and glad the demo resonated.

Summary / proposed MAP (high level):
1) Week 0 (this week): sign MAP + org seed
   - Deliverable: signed MAP (DocuSign) and org admin email added to Redwood Console
2) Week 1: credentials & connectivity
   - Deliverable: ephemeral API key + service account for load testing, IP allowlist configured for ClearHealth CI runners, VPC peering request submitted and initial routing validated
3) Week 2: smoke tests + perf run
   - Deliverable: 48–72 hour load run against representative traffic, token-cost baseline, latency SLO check
4) Week 3: acceptance & close
   - Deliverable: acceptance sign-off or scope for next phase

To move forward I need the following from ClearHealth: org admin email, preferred AWS region, and the CIDR/IPs you plan to allow from your side. Ive attached our typical MAP template (redwood-map-template.xlsx) and included a DocuSign link we usually use (https://www.docusign.net/clearhealth-map) for quick signature.

Notes on keys: by default we provision a short-lived API key for test load (90d) and recommend a service account with limited scopes for sustained evaluation. If you need HSM/KMS integration we can scope that in the private deployment workstream.

Karthik, can you call out the minimal routing/security items we should ask ClearHealth to prepare (CIDRs, AWS account IDs, required ports)? Aditya, Ill sync with you on the customer-facing timeline and can own the MAP doc.

Next step: Priya — if you can provide org-admin and CIDRs today well put the MAP in DocuSign and begin key provisioning tomorrow.

Thanks,

Soojin Lee

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC planning — environment steps and timeline

Thanks for the tag, Soojin. Technical checklist for ClearHealth (minimum to start):

- VPC peering (AWS):
  - Our side: Redwood will supply VPC id and account for the peering request (we typically use a managed peering edge per-customer).
  - Your side: please open peering in AWS console for account 987654321012 -> requester account we provide. Share the VPC ID (one /24 or larger) and route table IDs to update.
  - Routing: add route to our peering CIDR; we require 0.0.0.0/0 egress to internet for model downloads only, otherwise traffic will be direct via peering for inference calls.
- IP allowlist: provide the list of public egress IPs from your CI/load runners (we will add to firewall). If you cannot provide static egress IPs we can accept a temporary tunnel (NGROK-style) for the load run but this complicates acceptance.
- Ports: 443 outbound (TLS) for inference; 22/443 for any admin bastion if you want direct connectivity for troubleshooting (optional).
- API keys: we will create two keys:
  - test-key-<id>: short-lived default for load tests (90d)
  - svc-account-<id>: long-lived for automation (rotated quarterly)
  - Both keys are bound to the org and can be scoped by model and rate-limits.
- Security evidence: we will need a primary contact for SOC/infosec questions and the earliest date for a light questionnaire.

I attached a short VPC peering checklist with the exact AWS console steps we recommend. I can run the peering request once I get the VPC ID and the AWS account contact.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
